LESSON: FABRIC DECORATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.2: Fabric Decoration
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fabric Decoration, part of Performing and Displaying in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is fabric decoration important? 2.What are the sources of natural dyes?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify tie and dye techniques in fabric decoration,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fabric Decoration in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify fabric decorated using applique technique,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fabric Decoration in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. decorate a fabric using tie and dye techniques for skill acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fabric Decoration in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. applique to decorate a fabric for expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fabric Decoration in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify tie and dye techniques in fabric decoration,

   Fabric Decoration helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. identify fabric decorated using applique technique,

   Fabric Decoration helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. decorate a fabric using tie and dye techniques for skill acquisition,

   Fabric Decoration helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. applique to decorate a fabric for expression,

   Fabric Decoration helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fabric Decoration together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Digital literacy: The learner explores virtual and actual sources to study techniques of fabric decoration

 Creativity and imagination: The learner decorates the fabric using applique technique

29

Values:
 Love: The learner portrays a caring attitude while working together in decorate a fabric using tie and dye techniques

 Responsibility: The learner handles tools for decorating fabrics by trimming and ironing

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

 Social cohesion: The learner talks about own and others work in a just manner.

 environmental conservation :The learner sources materials such as recyclable fabrics, tying/stitching/pasting

Link to other learning areas:

Agriculture and nutrition: The learner studies techniques of fabric decoration focusing on; tie and dye, applique and materials in

fabric decoration
